terms.definition: Standing upright, facing forward, feet flat and parallel, arms at the sides with palms facing forward; the reference posture for all directional terms.
Superior means toward the head (above); inferior means toward the feet (below).
Anterior (ventral) means toward the front of the body; posterior (dorsal) means toward the back.
Medial means toward the midline of the body; lateral means away from the midline.
Proximal means closer to the point of attachment or origin (the trunk, for a limb); distal means farther from it.
A vertical plane dividing the body into left and right parts; the midsagittal plane divides it into equal halves.
A vertical plane dividing the body into anterior and posterior parts.
A horizontal plane dividing the body into superior and inferior parts.
Epithelial, connective, muscle, and nervous tissue.
Integumentary, skeletal, muscular, nervous, endocrine, cardiovascular, lymphatic/immune, respiratory, digestive, urinary, and reproductive.
The skull, vertebral column, and thoracic cage (ribs and sternum); an adult has 80 bones in the axial skeleton.
The bones of the limbs plus the pectoral and pelvic girdles; an adult has 126 bones in the appendicular skeleton.

terms.term: Number of bones in the adult human skeleton

terms.definition: The thigh bone; the longest and strongest bone in the body.
The vertebral column has 7 cervical, 12 thoracic, and 5 lumbar vertebrae, followed by the sacrum and coccyx.
Skeletal (voluntary, striated), cardiac (involuntary, striated), and smooth (involuntary, non-striated).
The agonist (prime mover) produces a movement; the antagonist opposes it, as the triceps opposes the biceps at the elbow.
A tendon connects muscle to bone; a ligament connects bone to bone.
Right atrium, right ventricle, left atrium, and left ventricle.

terms.term: Path of blood through the heart
terms.definition: Body to right atrium, right ventricle, lungs via the pulmonary arteries, left atrium, left ventricle, then out to the body via the aorta.
Arteries carry blood away from the heart; veins carry blood toward the heart.
The dome-shaped skeletal muscle beneath the lungs whose contraction drives inspiration.
Tiny air sacs in the lungs where gas exchange between air and blood occurs.
The central nervous system is the brain and spinal cord; the peripheral nervous system is all the nerves outside them.
A nerve cell, made up of a cell body (soma), dendrites that receive signals, and an axon that transmits them.
Frontal, parietal, temporal, and occipital.
Duodenum, jejunum, and ileum.
The nephron; each kidney contains roughly one million of them.
The skin (integumentary system).
